headline: Occupancy stabilizes but margin pressure widens the net loss
summary_short: Lineage's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 0.8% y/y to $1,361 million, but adjusted EBITDA fell 1.8% to $320 million (per the company's own reconciliation) and the GAAP net loss attributable to Lineage widened to $29 million from $6 million a year ago, even as same-warehouse physical occupancy improved 90bps y/y.
summary_long: Revenue growth came almost entirely from non-same warehouses (+45.6% segment revenue on new sites); same-warehouse revenue grew just 0.4% as storage revenue per pallet fell despite higher occupancy. Adjusted EBITDA fell 1.8% y/y to $320M (margin -60bps to 23.5%) and AFFO/share fell 6.2% to $0.76. GAAP net loss widened to $29M from $6M on $87M of interest expense (vs $67M) and no repeat of last year's $26M FX gain, partly offset by lower acquisition costs. Cash fell to $58M from $82M as H1 dividends and capex outspent operating cash flow; long-term debt rose 8.5% y/y to $6,220M on net revolver draws. FY2026 guidance stands at $1.26-1.29B adjusted EBITDA and $2.80-3.05 AFFO/share, with no prior range stated.

drivers.explanation: Growth came almost entirely from non-same warehouses (+45.6% revenue, +159.7% throughput pallets on new/expanded sites); same warehouse revenue grew just 0.4% as storage revenue per pallet fell despite higher occupancy, and Global Integrated Solutions revenue fell 6.3%.
Global warehousing segment margin fell 130bps to 36.5% as labor costs rose 6.3% and power costs rose 7.8%, outpacing the segment's 3.6% revenue growth.
Rose as one-time costs fell: $37M of acquisition/transaction expense in Q2 2025 did not recur, and restructuring/impairment/disposal activity swung to a $4M net gain from a $3M expense a year ago.
Loss widened y/y mainly on interest expense of $87M (vs $67M) and the absence of a $26M FX transaction gain booked in Q2 2025, partly offsetting the improvement in operating income.
Cash fell to $58M as H1 financing outflows ($269M of dividends) and $310M of capex/investing outflows outpaced $441M of operating cash flow for the six months ended June 30, 2026.
Debt rose 8.5% y/y mainly from net revolver draws ($1,063M borrowed vs $736M repaid in H1 2026) funding acquisitions and expansion capex, since no new long-term notes were issued this year.

CEO Greg Lehmkuhl called Q2 'solid,' citing a 90bps y/y increase in same-warehouse physical occupancy as a sign of inventory normalization and industry stabilization, while also acknowledging a fire at the Big Bear facility during the quarter.
